senses.text: to bind by prefixing a quantifier
to make explicit the logical quantity of
to determine, express, or measure the quantity of

entries.history: Medieval Latin quantificare, from Latin quantus how much

senses.text: a unit of capacity equal to 1/4 gallon or 1/32 bushel — see Weights and Measures Table
a vessel or measure having a capacity of one quart

entries.history: Middle English, from Anglo-French quarte quarter, quart, from feminine of quart, adjective, fourth, from Latin quartus; akin to Latin quattuor four — more at four

phrases.meaning: bad quarter hour : an uncomfortable though brief experience

senses.text: a spirited march tune usually accompanying a march in quick time
having many quirks unusual in especially an interesting or appealing way

senses.also: especially the share or proportion assigned to each in a division or to each member of a body

senses.text: the number or amount constituting a proportional share
a fixed number or percentage of minority group members or women needed to meet the requirements of affirmative action

entries.history: Medieval Latin, from Latin quota pars how great a part
